title: GEAS 10-01 Mastery Challenge: Legislative Origins, Articles & Terms
description: Comprehensive 25-item decoupled board examination challenge covering statutory enactment facts, the 8 Articles, 43 Sections, and Section 3 definitions under Republic Act No. 9292.

questions.promptText: What is the official short title of Republic Act No. 9292 as stated in Section 1?
questions.choiceA: Electronics and Communications Engineering Act of 2004
questions.choiceD: Professional Electronics Practice Code of the Philippines
questions.explanation: Section 1 states: 'This Act shall be known as the Electronics Engineering Law of 2004.' Notice that 'Communications' was dropped from the official short title.

questions.promptText: On what exact date was Republic Act No. 9292 signed into law by the President of the Philippines?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 9292 was approved on April 17, 2004. (June 21, 1969 was the approval date of the repealed R.A. 5734).

questions.promptText: Which Republic Act was repealed and superseded upon the passage of Republic Act No. 9292?
questions.explanation: R.A. 5734 (The Electronics and Communications Engineering Act of the Philippines, enacted June 21, 1969) was repealed by Section 42 of R.A. 9292.

questions.promptText: Republic Act No. 9292 was a consolidation of which legislative measures in the 12th Congress?
questions.choiceA: House Bill No. 5224 and Senate Bill No. 2683
questions.choiceB: House Bill No. 2683 and Senate Bill No. 5224
questions.choiceC: House Bill No. 1096 and Senate Bill No. 3846
questions.choiceD: House Bill No. 7925 and Senate Bill No. 8484
questions.explanation: R.A. 9292 originated from House Bill No. 5224 and Senate Bill No. 2683.

questions.promptText: Who was the Senate President who signed the enrolled copy of Republic Act No. 9292?
questions.explanation: Franklin M. Drilon was the Senate President, while Jose De Venecia Jr. was the Speaker of the House.

questions.promptText: How many Articles and Sections comprise Republic Act No. 9292?
questions.explanation: Republic Act No. 9292 contains 8 Articles and 43 Sections.

questions.promptText: Which Article of R.A. 9292 covers 'Examination, Registration and Licensure'?
questions.explanation: Article III (Sections 13 to 26) is dedicated to Examination, Registration and Licensure.

questions.promptText: Under what Article of R.A. 9292 is the creation, composition, and powers of the Professional Regulatory Board of Electronics Engineering specified?
questions.explanation: Article II (Sections 6 to 12) governs the Professional Regulatory Board of Electronics Engineering.

questions.promptText: Under Section 3(a) of R.A. 9292, which carrier of electric charge or media is explicitly mentioned in the statutory definition of Electronics?
questions.choiceB: Metallic wires and coaxial shields only
questions.choiceD: Vacuum, gaseous media, plasma, semiconductors, or any other media
questions.explanation: Section 3(a) defines Electronics as dealing with electron flow in vacuum, in gaseous media, in plasma, in semiconductors, or in any other media.

questions.promptText: How does Section 3(e) of R.A. 9292 legally define a 'Computer'?
questions.choiceA: Any electronic device capable of accepting data, executing programs/instructions, and presenting results
questions.choiceB: A mechanical device calculating mathematical matrices using decimal gears
questions.choiceC: Any network server hosting website protocols over TCP/IP
questions.choiceD: A cellular handset operating over 3G/4G telecommunications spectrum
questions.explanation: Section 3(e) defines a Computer as any of a variety of electronic devices capable of accepting data, programs/instructions, executing them to process data, and presenting results.

questions.promptText: Under Section 3(f), what processes define 'Information and Communications Technology (ICT)'?
questions.choiceA: Manufacturing of copper cables and circuit boards only
questions.choiceB: Acquisition, production, transformation, storage, and transfer/transmission of data and information
questions.choiceC: Broadcasting of analog frequency modulated audio signals only
questions.choiceD: Installation of fiber optic underwater cable lines only
questions.explanation: Section 3(f) states that ICT is the acquisition, production, transformation, storage and transfer/transmission of data and info by electronic and other modern means.

questions.promptText: What is the key statutory phrase that distinguishes 'Broadcasting' from other forms of telecommunications in Section 3(i)?
questions.choiceC: Intended for the reception of the general public
questions.explanation: Section 3(i) defines Broadcasting as an undertaking transmitting audio, video, text, or images 'for reception of the general public'.

questions.promptText: Under Section 3(j), what constitutes an 'Industrial Plant'?
questions.choiceA: Manufacturing establishments and businesses where electronic machineries/equipment are installed, used, sold, operated, etc.
questions.choiceB: Retail shopping malls and restaurants only
questions.explanation: Section 3(j) defines Industrial Plant as manufacturing establishments and businesses where electronic machineries/equipment are installed, used, sold, operated, etc.

questions.promptText: What are 'Consulting Services' as defined in Section 3(l) of R.A. 9292?
questions.choiceA: Routine soldering and assembly line repair
questions.choiceB: Services requiring technical expertise and professional capability for advisory, review, design, and evaluation
questions.choiceC: Retail counter sales of electronics components
questions.choiceD: Clerical filing of board exam records
questions.explanation: Section 3(l) defines Consulting Services as services involving technical expertise and professional capability for advisory, review, design, evaluation, planning, or supervision.

questions.promptText: Which Section of R.A. 9292 contains the General Penal Provisions?
questions.explanation: Section 35 under Article VI prescribes the fines (₱100k to ₱1M) and imprisonment terms (6 months to 6 years).

questions.promptText: Which Section defines the 'Categories of Practice' under R.A. 9292?
questions.explanation: Section 4 (under Article I) establishes the 3 categories of practice: PECE, ECE, and ECT.

questions.promptText: Which Article contains 'Sundry Provisions', including the Accredited Professional Organization (APO) and Foreign Reciprocity?
questions.explanation: Article V (Sections 32 to 34) contains the Sundry Provisions.

questions.promptText: What does Section 41 of R.A. 9292 provide?
questions.explanation: Section 41 is the Separability Clause (if any section is declared unconstitutional, the remainder stays valid). Section 42 is Repealing, Section 43 is Effectivity.

questions.promptText: What is the Effectivity period specified in Section 43 of R.A. 9292?
questions.choiceA: Immediately upon signature of the President
questions.choiceB: 30 days after registration with the United Nations
questions.choiceD: 15 days following its full publication in the Official Gazette or two newspapers of general circulation
questions.explanation: Section 43 states effectivity takes place 15 days following full publication in the Official Gazette or at least two newspapers of general circulation.

questions.promptText: What is the title of Article VII of R.A. 9292?
questions.explanation: Article VII comprises Sections 37 and 38 and is titled 'Transitory Provisions'.

questions.promptText: Under Section 38 (Vested Rights), what happened to all registered Electronics and Communications Engineers (ECEs) upon enactment of R.A. 9292?
questions.choiceA: They were required to retake the licensure examination within 1 year
questions.choiceB: They were automatically upgraded to Professional Electronics Engineers (PECE)
questions.choiceC: They were automatically converted into Electronics Engineers (ECEs)
questions.choiceD: Their licenses were cancelled until they completed a Master's degree
questions.explanation: Section 38 explicitly protects vested rights: all existing ECEs under RA 5734 automatically became registered Electronics Engineers under RA 9292.

questions.promptText: Which Section governs the 'Code of Ethics and Code of Technical Standard of Practice'?
questions.explanation: Section 30 (Article IV) states that the Board shall adopt a Code of Ethics and Code of Technical Standards of Practice promulgated by the Accredited Professional Organization.

questions.promptText: Under Section 3(k), how is a 'Commercial Establishment' defined?
questions.choiceA: Buildings used for business or profit where electronic or electronically-controlled equipment are installed, used, sold, operated, etc.
questions.choiceB: Private residential houses with home appliances
questions.choiceC: Farming lands and open irrigation canals
questions.explanation: Section 3(k) defines Commercial Establishment as buildings used for business or profit where electronic equipment/circuits are installed, operated, or sold.

questions.promptText: Who attested the enrolled copy of R.A. 9292 as Secretary General of the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: Roberto P. Nazareno was Secretary General of the House, while Oscar G. Yabes was Secretary of the Senate.

questions.promptText: Under Section 3(g), how is 'Communications' defined?
questions.choiceA: Oral conversation between people in the same room only
questions.choiceC: Mechanical semaphore flags on naval ships only
questions.choiceD: The process of sending and/or receiving information, data, message, etc. between two or more points by any media
questions.explanation: Section 3(g) defines Communications as the process of sending and/or receiving information, data, message, etc. between two or more points by any media.
